title: Levocetirizine
overview: On May 16, 2025, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued a drug safety communication warning about a rare risk of severe itching that can occur after stopping long-term use of oral allergy medications, such as levocetirizine. Most patients who experienced itching after stopping the drug, had been taking the drug for 3 months or longer. Although some had taken for less than 1 month. Patients should contact their healthcare provider if they develop severe itching after stopping cetirizine. For additional information see: https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-safety-and-availability/fda-requires-warning-about-rare-severe-itching-after-stopping-long-term-use-oral-allergy-medicines?utm_medium=email&utm_source=govdelivery

sections.Before taking levocetirizine,: tell your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to this medication, any part of this medication, or any other medications, foods or substances. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about the allergy and what symptoms you had. or any other medications.tell your doctor and pharmacist what other prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking or plan to take while taking levocetirizine. Your doctor may need to change the doses of your medications or monitor you carefully for side effects.tell your doctor if you have or ever have had kidney disease.tell your doctor if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant. If you become pregnant while taking levocetirizine, call your doctor. Do not breast-feed while you are taking levocetirizine.you should know that levocetirizine may make you drowsy. Do not drive a car or operate machinery until you know how this medication affects you.ask your doctor about the safe use of alcoholic beverages while you are taking levocetirizine. Alcohol can add to the drowsiness caused by this medication.you should know that you could develop severe itching within a few days after you stop taking levocetirizine. This can happen after you have been taking regularly for a few months or years. Talk to your doctor if you have any questions about risks associated with long-term use of levocetirizine products.
